lesson.grammar_point: language of scope and definition: defining a term (X means, X refers to, X is defined as, for the purposes of) and widening or narrowing the scope (including but not limited to, limited to, excluding, in relation to, to the extent that, falls within or outside the scope of)

listenings.text: I've managed software projects for almost twenty years, and I can tell you exactly how most of them fail. It isn't one big mistake. It's a hundred small requests. Someone asks for one extra report. Then a new button. Then a version for the sales team, just a small one. Every request sounds reasonable on its own, and nobody wants to say no in a meeting. Six months later, the project is twice as big, the budget is the same, and everyone is angry. We call it scope creep. The cure is boring, but it works. Before we start, we write down what the project includes, and, just as important, what it doesn't include. We define the words that people will argue about later, like finished, or tested, or live. And when a new request comes in, we don't say no. We say, that's outside the current scope, so let's estimate it as a change. People are surprisingly happy with that answer.

I've been renovating kitchens for twenty-five years, and the most expensive word in my business is everything. A client says, I want you to do everything. Does that include the floor? The lights? Moving the sink to the other wall? So I never start a job without a one-page scope of work. It lists what's included, item by item, and then it lists what's excluded, because that's the part people forget. Painting the living room is excluded, even if the paint is already in the house. I also define finished. For me, finished means the kitchen works and has been cleaned, not that every cabinet handle is the one you saw online last week. My clients sometimes think the paper is a little cold. But when we disagree in the third week, and we always disagree in the third week, nobody has to remember what anybody said. We just read the page together, and we usually agree in five minutes.

reading.rtitle: Terms of Reference (extract) -- Lumen Varejo S.A. v. Orbis Systems Inc.
paras: 1. Definitions. For the purposes of these Terms of Reference, “the Agreement” means the Software Implementation Agreement signed by the Parties on 3 March 2025. “The System” refers to the retail management software described in Schedule 1 to the Agreement. “The Go-Live Date” is defined as the date on which the System is first used in all of the Claimant’s 140 stores.

2. The Tribunal’s remit. The Tribunal shall decide all disputes arising out of or in relation to the Agreement, including but not limited to the disputes over delay, payment and quality. Its remit does not extend to the separate maintenance contract of 2023, which contains its own dispute clause and falls outside the scope of this arbitration.

3. The Parties’ positions. The Claimant contends that the System was delivered fourteen months late, and claims damages of USD 6.2 million. The Respondent maintains that the delay was caused by more than ninety change requests from the Claimant, which, in its view, turned a twelve-month project into a different project altogether. This summary is not exhaustive, and the Parties’ full written submissions prevail.

4. Issues to be determined. The issues include, inter alia: (a) whether the change requests fall within the scope of the Agreement, as described in Schedule 1; (b) to what extent, if any, the Respondent is liable for the delay; and (c) whether the limitation of liability in Clause 18 applies. The Tribunal may add new issues only to the extent that they relate to the Agreement and both Parties have had an opportunity to comment.
reading.source: Alumni by Better -- B2 reading, written for this lesson as a realistic extract of Terms of Reference (the case, the companies and the people are fictional)

reading.prompt: What is the main purpose of this document?
choices: To decide who is responsible for the delay, and how much the Respondent must pay the Claimant for the fourteen months.
To fix what the key words mean, what the tribunal can decide and which questions it will answer.
To replace the Software Implementation Agreement.

items: The Tribunal can decide disputes about the 2023 maintenance contract.
Paragraph 2: that contract falls outside the scope of this arbitration.
Delay, payment and quality are the only disputes the Tribunal can decide.
Paragraph 2: including but not limited to -- the list is open.
The Tribunal has already decided that the change requests caused the delay.
Paragraph 3: the Respondent only maintains it. Paragraph 4: it is still an issue to be determined.
“The Go-Live Date” has one precise meaning in this document.
Paragraph 1: it is defined as the date on which the System is first used in all 140 stores.
